thesis: Shaytan's aim in the Garden was not merely to make Adam and his wife break a rule but to strip away the covering Allah had mercifully placed over them, and the approach to the boundary (la taqraba) is where the collapse actually begins.
notes: CLEAN ON THE KNOWN RISK. This file carries NONE of the isra'iliyyat that had to be repaired out of the sibling 007-al-araf/ayahs-023-025.md. Checked explicitly and confirmed absent: no serpent/snake, no peacock, no identification of the tree (al-Jalalayn glosses it الحنطة/wheat and the file wisely stays silent), no claim that Hawwa' was tempted first or tempted Adam. The file never even names Hawwa' — it says 'his wife' throughout, matching the Qur'anic wording, and it keeps the dual throughout (fa-waswasa lahuma, qasamahuma, dallahuma), which is exactly the guard against the Hawwa'-first import. Thesis grounding: the exposure-reading is carried directly by the ayah's own purpose clause (li-yubdiya lahuma ma wuriya 'anhuma) and by Ibn Kathir ('He wished to rid them of the various favors and nice clothes that they were enjoying') and al-Tabari ('li-yubdiya lahuma ma wuriya 'anhuma min saw'atihima ... ma warahu Allah 'anhuma min 'awratihima fa-ghattahu bi-sitrihi'). Morphology verified against scripts/.corpus-cache/quranic-corpus.json: 7:20 yubdiya = VF:4 root بدو; wuriya = VF:3 PASSIVE root وري (file's 'what had been hidden, screened, covered over' is correct); 7:22 dhaqa = 3MD dual, tafiqa = 3MD, yakhsifani = 3MD root خصف. No countable/absolute claims in the file at all — nothing of the 'exactly N times / the only place / hapax' kind — so there was nothing for a count-check to fail on. Two cosmetic imprecisions not worth a flag: (1) the file calls 7:21 'the verb qasama' when the form is qasama Form III (mutual-oath form), though Ibn Kathir's gloss 'swore to them both by Allah' supports the file's reading; (2) 'one of the Qur'an's recurring ways' re la taqraba is loose but true (cf. 6:152, 17:32, 17:34). No fix required.

thesis: When transgression becomes communal culture, purity itself begins to look like provocation — so the people of Lut answered a prophet not with argument but with expulsion, naming his followers' self-purification as the offense.

flags.quote: It is portraying desire that overran its boundary and then demanded public legitimacy.
flags.issue: Not in the passage and not in any of the four fetched editions. The ayah reports the people's jawab as akhrijuhum min qaryatikum — expulsion — not a demand for legitimation. al-Tabari glosses musrifun narrowly: 'innakum la-qawmun ta'tuna ma harrama Allahu 'alaykum wa ta'sunahu bi-fi'likum hadha'. al-Jalalayn: 'mutajawizuna al-halala ila al-haram'. al-Muyassar: 'mutajawizuna li-hududi Allah fi al-israf fi al-ma'asi wa'l-shahawat'. None carries a legitimacy-seeking element. This is asserted as what the ayah 'is portraying', not offered as contemplation, so it fails rubric 1 as an unflagged interpolation.

flags.quote: Over time it wants moral reversal. It wants language changed, shame displaced, standards mocked, and purity treated as aggression.
flags.issue: Only the last clause is grounded — Qatadah in Ibn Kathir and al-Tabari: ''abuhum bi-ghayri 'ayb wa dhammuhum bi-ghayri dhamm' (they shamed them with what is no shame at all). 'Wants language changed' and 'standards mocked' have no basis in any of the four editions and are a present-tense sociological program read into a narrative that names only one act and one response. Combined with the section title 'Public Sin Eventually Demands Public Moral Inversion' and the closing 'There is a point of moral decline at which people stop merely resisting truth and begin resenting those who still wish to live by it', the file builds a contemporary-application frame on the single most adversarially-quotable passage in the corpus, with no classical anchor and no reflection flag.

flags.quote: So when the ayah closes with *musrifun*, it teaches that sin is not only about the object chosen but about the transgressive relation to desire itself.
flags.issue: Rubric 4 failure — the file has NO tadabbur-vs-fatwa line and no scope statement anywhere, despite being the most ahkam-adjacent passage in this group. Ibn Kathir's own commentary on 7:83-84 closes with the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas (Ahmad, Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah) prescribing death for the doer and the one done to, and the punishment for liwat is a live classical ikhtilaf. The file neither states a ruling (good) nor disclaims one (the gap). Because it does spend its Thematic Depths section on present-day moral application, a reader — or a hostile quoter — has nothing in the file marking where reflection stops and fiqh begins.

flags.quote: It says they are **working at purity**, actively making themselves pure. The form itself carries the image of sustained effort — someone bending their life toward cleanliness as a daily practice.
flags.issue: The morphology is correct — corpus confirms 7:82 يتطهرون as VF:5 root طهر — but the semantic expansion runs past the commentators. Every fetched gloss reads it as abstention from the specific act, not a general program of cleanliness: al-Tabari 'yatanazzahuna 'amma naf'aluhu nahnu min ityani al-rijali fi al-adbar', Mujahid and Ibn 'Abbas 'min adbari al-rijali wa adbari al-nisa'', as-Suddi 'yataharrajun', al-Muyassar and al-Jalalayn the same. Generalization, not a false claim — minor.

notes: The thesis itself is sound and well-grounded (Qatadah's ''abuhum bi-ghayri 'ayb' carries it exactly), and the file is CLEAN on the isra'iliyyat risk: no naming or elaboration of the cities, no graphic detail, no Lut-and-his-daughters material, no modern group named or implied by name. Verified mechanically: 7:84 amtarna = VF:4 root مطر and mataran = root مطر, so 'the repetition of the rain-root in verb and noun' is TRUE; 7:82 yatatahharun = VF:5, TRUE. So this is not a false-thesis flag — it is an adab-and-framing flag, and the fix is small and surgical. SPECIFIC FIX: (1) delete or reflection-mark 'and then demanded public legitimacy' and the 'wants language changed, shame displaced, standards mocked' clause — keeping 'purity treated as aggression', which Qatadah supports; (2) add the scope line the sibling file already models. 007-al-araf/ayahs-031-032.md does this well and should be copied in register: '...is the work of fiqh ... Tadabbur is not the place to settle it, and this reflection is not attempting to.' One equivalent sentence, placed before or inside Theme 1, closes the rubric-4 gap without touching the passage's moral clarity. ALSO NOTE (metadata, non-blocking): this file's frontmatter is missing the `concepts:` field that all three sibling files in this group carry, and `validated: false`.

thesis: 7:31-32 corrects one community erring in two opposite directions at once — too little covering in worship and too many self-invented food prohibitions — so Allah neither sanctifies ugliness nor licenses appetite, but teaches adornment and provision to be received lawfully, gratefully and without israf.
notes: STRONGEST FILE IN THIS GROUP, and it clears the ahkam risk the brief flagged. Every tafsir attribution checks out verbatim against the fetched editions: Ibn Kathir's refutation of naked tawaf with the Ibn 'Abbas report through Muslim/an-Nasa'i/Ibn Jarir, men by day and women by night — VERIFIED; at-Tabari's double-audience description 'alladhina yata'arrawna 'inda tawafihim bi-baytihi al-haram ... wa'l-muharrimina minhum akla ma lam yuharrimhu Allahu 'alayhim min halali rizqihi, tabarruran 'inda nafsihi li-rabbihi' — VERIFIED, and the file's rendering 'as an act of piety in their own estimation' is an accurate translation of tabarruran 'inda nafsihi; at-Tabari's zinah gloss 'min al-kisa' wa'l-libas' — VERIFIED; al-Muyassar's 'al-zinah al-mashru'ah min thiyab satirah li-'awratikum wa nazafah wa taharah' and his 'al-musrifina fi al-ta'ami wa'l-sharabi WA GHAYRI DHALIK' (the file's 'and in other than that') — VERIFIED; Ibn Kathir on 7:32 'refutes those who prohibit any type of food, drink or clothes according to their own understanding, without relying on what Allah has legislated' — VERIFIED verbatim; al-Muyassar on khalisah, that others share it with believers in dunya — VERIFIED. THE LOAD-BEARING ONE: the file claims 'at-Tabari himself records that the early scholars differed over the referent of tayyibat'. at-Tabari's text reads 'wa-khtalafa ahlu al-ta'wili fi al-ma'niyyi bi-al-tayyibati mina al-rizqi, ba'da ijma'ihim 'anna al-zinata ma qulna' and then lays out the lahm/wadak view (as-Suddi, Ibn Zayd) against the bahirah/sa'ibah/wasilah/ham view (Qatadah, Ibn 'Abbas) — VERIFIED EXACTLY, including the file's implicit point that they agreed on zinah while differing on tayyibat. Morphology all verified in corpus: harrama VF:2 (Form II), akhraja VF:4 (Form IV), la tusrifu VF:4 root سرف, al-musrifin ACT_PCPL VF:4 same root (the file's verb-to-participle observation is exactly right), nufassilu VF:2 root فصل, khalisatan root خلص. RUBRIC 4 IS AFFIRMATIVELY SATISFIED, not merely not-violated: the file states no dress or consumption ruling, and explicitly holds the line — 'where the boundaries actually fall — what counts among the tayyibat, what a garment may be, what crosses into israf in a particular life — is the work of fiqh ... Tadabbur is not the place to settle it, and this reflection is not attempting to.' It also explicitly refuses to supply a quantity ('no count of mouthfuls, no ceiling on what a garment may cost'). It does NOT assert what the sibling 007-al-araf/ayahs-026-027.md hedges. ONE MINOR IMPRECISION, no fix required: the file says 'Ibn Kathir and at-Tabari anchor the phrase to its immediate occasion, the Sacred House and the tawaf' — Ibn Kathir does anchor it there but ALSO extends it ('people were commanded to wear their best clothes when performing every prayer'; 'encourage wearing the best clothes when praying, especially for Friday and 'Id'), and al-Jalalayn gives both ('inda al-salati wa'l-tawaf). The file understates Ibn Kathir's reach but does not misstate him, and its next line ('The two readings are not at war') describes what Ibn Kathir actually does.

thesis: After demolishing invented prohibitions, the surah names the actual forbidden things so that people reorder their moral attention before their appointed term arrives, and once the signs are recited the soul goes either to taqwa-and-repair or to denial-and-arrogance.
notes: Clean on both risks the brief named. (1) MA LAM YUNAZZIL BIHI SULTANAN IS NOT STRETCHED. The file says only 'Shirk is exposed not only as false worship but as worship without revealed warrant. There is no descending proof for it.' That matches at-Tabari ('lam yaj'al lakum fi ishrakikum iyyahu fi 'ibadatihi hujjatan wa la burhanan, wa huwa al-sultan') and al-Jalalayn ('sultanan — hujjah'). Critically, the file does NOT run the phrase outward into the dangerous generalization that anything lacking an explicit revealed text is thereby shirk or forbidden, and its 'not only ... but' construction preserves that shirk is wrong in itself. (2) THE LIST IS NOT TURNED INTO A FATWA. No ruling is issued anywhere; the file's use of the innama restriction stays inside at-Tabari's own framing ('inna Allaha lam yuharrim ma tuharrimunahu, bal ahalla dhalika li-'ibadihi al-mu'minina wa tayyabahu lahum, wa innama harrama rabbi al-qaba'iha mina al-ashya''). The one place this could have gone wrong — reading innama as making the five-item list exhaustive of all haram — the file avoids: it says 'Not everything people dramatize as sacred boundary is actually one' and 'Before multiplying taboos, listen to what Allah actually named', which is a claim about misplaced attention, not about exhaustiveness. Other attributions verified: ithm as sin against oneself vs baghy as transgression against others matches Ibn Kathir (as-Suddi and Mujahid); the two-destination fork matches Ibn Kathir on 7:35-36 and al-Tabari on 7:36; 'communities have appointed terms' matches at-Tabari on 7:34 ('li-kulli jama'atin ijtama'at 'ala takdhibi rusuli Allah ... ajal') and Ibn Kathir ('each generation and nation'). No countable, hapax, 'only place' or 'first' claims anywhere in the file, so nothing required a corpus count. ONE MINOR LOOSENESS the reviewer may want to tighten but which is not an error: 'The list closes where the previous passage also warned us to fear most' — the qawl-'ala-Allah warning is at 7:28, not in the immediately preceding 7:31-32 tadabbur file. It is defensible as written, because at-Tabari and al-Muyassar both gloss 'say about Allah what you do not know' precisely as the invented clothing/food prohibitions that 7:31-32 addressed, which is the connection the file is reaching for.
